options.misconception: dismisses metric
reads the evidence as Jobs cost nothing instead of Each job costs the public 80.
it overlooks the cost the item explicitly builds in

questions.explanation: Cost per job of 80 means each job costs the public 80. Denying cost misreads the metric. A reasonable-sounding guess, "Cost is irrelevant" is a seductive distractor: it dismisses metric. Easy to pick on a quick read, "Each job is free" fails on closer inspection: it overlooks the cost the item explicitly builds in. Superficially appealing, "Jobs cost nothing" is a common wrong turn: it ignores cost.
